namespaces.notes: The only secret-shaped fields are keystore:// references, which are inert on another machine.

A bare https URL with no userinfo and no credential in the query (urlRef holds a token-bearing address), plus a headersRef. Legacy RuleListProfile headers are the SEC-1 counter-example (omega-target/src/options.coffee:27).
The one namespace carrying raw payload. Never sync-eligible, hard-expiring, and the only place the secretBearing rule above is non-vacuous.

A pre-migration snapshot is a copy of everything, so it inherits the secrets it copied. Local-only, and the migration runner refuses to run without one (docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §7).

secretReferences.mintedBy: The Connector, when it stores a value: it generates a random identifier and returns keystore://<entity>/<that identifier>/<field>. Nothing in the extension, the envelope or a feed ever composes a reference, and no part of the stored value is ever part of one.
neverDerivedFrom: the secret value itself -- a content-addressed reference is an offline dictionary: the reference syncs, exports and logs freely, so a guesser only compares strings
any digest, truncated digest or keyed MAC of the secret value
the entity display name, address or port, which are all public and would put the field's meaning in the identifier

fields.name: user-id
fields.description: The VLESS user id (a UUID). Server.userIdRef and the compiled Core client both point here.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: A header map carrying Authorization, Cookie or an API key -- for a transport (ws/grpc/xhttp) or for a subscription feed. Names are displayable, values are not, so the map's keys survive masking and its values never do.

fields.name: url
fields.description: A fetch address whose query or path is a credential. SubscriptionSource.urlRef; nothing of the value is ever shown, because the UI shows `url` -- the same address with its query dropped (docs/architecture/29 §4). A head-then-tail rule would be wrong here even for high entropy: the tail of such a URL is the token.

fields.name: token
fields.description: A single human-or-service credential: a sync-backend token (GitHub Gist, WebDAV -- SEC-5) or a passphrase for an upstream proxy imported from a legacy backup. Low entropy is the default assumption: a credential the user can read aloud has no partial display.

atRest.blobs: One DPAPI-protected blob per secret under the Connector's per-user keystore directory (ADR-0011 rule 1); the blob is the only place a value exists on disk.
atRest.compiledConfigLifetime: from the rename that installs it until core.stop or Connector shutdown; always re-derivable from intent plus keystore, so never backed up
